title: FOOTBALL | Jeff Lebby Press Conference - 11/14/26
text: Coach a couple in the beginning you kind of got exactly what you wanted. You got the style, [snorts] got the ball in midfield and you have the botched hold there. It just seems like the game's kind of playing you tough. What what can you do to make these things a little bit easier for the team? >> Yeah, I mean those things that happened at the beginning of the game again like we got to be able to go execute the field goal. We got to get the snap and snap's got to be better. We got to still be able to get the ball down and we got to be able to go knock it through to have momentum. Our football team needs the momentum and those moments to be able to go take advantage of having great field position, putting together a decent drive. We want touchdowns, but we have to be able to go execute and again so many areas that just they weren't it wasn't good enough and that the way we started very very frustrating. >> Obviously big news this week with Kamari announcing that he plans to come back. What what is your plan in the off season to kind of build around him to ensure that you don't have this type of situation should he go down next year with an ankle injury or something? >> Yeah, we're we're constantly evaluating our roster. We're constantly evaluating everything inside the program to make sure that we will be set up and ready to go and capitalize on having the best football player in college football and I've talked about building around him since we got him and that will be a huge piece of it as we move it forward. There's plenty of areas inside the program and from a retention standpoint and that we've got to address and those things will get addressed as we get get ready to finish out the regular season. We we need to go play really well these last two football games. That's the immediate, but again for me leading this program it is. It's about making sure we're looking at everything to put one in position to go have a great year to give us the ability to have that great year, but we need to go finish the right way these next two weeks. >> Just with those four fumbles that led to points for Auburn and a lot of the penalties that led to the field goal that they got to go up 10 nothing. What do you feel if you could find one connecting point with all of those things, what do you think those things all go back to? >> Yeah, I mean bad ball security. We we have to take care of the football. Those things can't happen. I believe it's 10-7 or 10-0 scoop score not scoop score, but they get to the 1 yd line. We come back and then put it on the ground again, give them an incredibly short field. They started on their side. Starting field position for them in the first quarter was just it was atrocious and really the first half and not good enough. And again, offensively not taking care of the football and giving these guys short fields was a recipe for disaster and that's exactly what happened. >> Are you worried that some of the players are starting to quit or maybe aren't giving their full effort in these games? >> No, I'm not worried about some of these guys trying to quit. I thought you look at the end of the game and the way we flew around defensively and fought to get off blocks and fought to go strain to go tackle and and make plays and continued to get off the field. So I I don't think that's part of it at all. I also think that when we're fourth and one in a situation, we need to be able to hand the football off and go score and and get the fourth and one to be able to stay on the field. So there's a lot of things that go into that. Bottom line is we've got to be able to go execute in those situations. So first part of it, absolutely not. Our our guys I feel none of that whatsoever. >> It's been a frustrating few weeks, but the three home games in particular, it's just felt like the home crowd's frustration and it's just built and built as what what's your message to them as to why you are the person to lead the team out of this? >> I really appreciative of our fan base today and how our our people showed up. Obviously with the time change and our people adjust in the way that they did to be able to be here at the beginning of the game. Incredibly proud to be able to walk out of that tunnel and see the crowd that we had. Really frustrated and disappointed that we don't play well enough to get them and keep them excited about how we're doing what we're doing. And again, for us, not good enough. Not good enough. And that's that's the bottom line. So again, I've talked about it already. We need to finish the right way. We need to respond the right way and go finish for this group on Saturday here at home. And then we all know what the what the next one looks like. So that's that's the immediate part of it. >> Do you feel pressure to to turn the ship around in these last two games in in terms of keeping this job for for next year? >> Yeah, for me, I I feel pressure from the standpoint of wanting to change the outcome. That's what I'm concerned with, the result on Saturday. And I'll that's what I'll always be concerned with and doing everything I possibly can to get our guys to go play well enough to go win the game. And that's my job and that that is what I'm concerned with every day is doing my job at a really high level to give our guys a chance to go win. >> Couple players that have kind of in during this losing streak that have really played well is Sam Frisco, McGee and and Fat Forest. I mean, you what are you getting from them? What are you It seems like Frisco's on in route to an all SEC caliber type year. I mean, despite all the challenges, what have you seen from those two guys that maybe have been bright spots? >> Yeah, I mean, Frisco has he's continued to get better and better. Talked about him in the spring and in fall camp and knew what he had the ability to be for us. That's showing up for us in a great way. Has to continue to play better and play cleaner in some situational things that will continue to help him and help us. But proud of him and just continuing to get better and better. Fat to me very very similar. A guy that again from right up the road that gets in here it took a little bit of time for him to find his footing and get on the field, but when he's had the opportunities this year he's played better and better. So uh excited about obviously both those guys as uh they've got years ahead and and how they're playing right now for us. >> Putting aside winning and losing because obviously the goal is for you guys is to win these next two games, what do you want to see from these next two games that you feel like will give confidence in the program in the people following the program that it's headed in the right direction? >> Yeah, we need to play clean football and especially offensively and taking great care of the ball. That that is what we have to see. That's what gives us a chance to go win and that again we are coaching for that result on Saturday and then we'll reset and understand again what the next one will be. But first and foremost we need to go play clean ball and that means taking great care of the ball every drive ending in a kick. That will give us a chance to win the game cuz I still believe defensively we're doing some really good things. >> Two parter. First is there any update on Swann and then also why did Brody McWhorter get a a few possessions there and then he went back to Pucket for most of the second half? >> Yeah, AJ I I don't have an update there. We'll we'll see uh how he bounces back and responds. I wanted to see which guy would give us the best opportunity inside the game. Um as some things happened in a couple of those drives Billy was going to give us the best chance to go operate and go get first downs and hopefully give us a chance to stay on the field. I gave gave Brody an opportunity cuz the ball was on the ground two times and in a couple of drives for for Billy and then again things went the way that they did and needed to get back to Billy to to give us a chance. >> Coach, three quarterbacks playing today. Um obviously none of them and I don't think anybody in the country can can kind of do what Kamari can, but have you have you considered changing maybe some style the way you play or any plays to fit the strength of who you guys have in that room that can play? >> Yeah, we're not still calling the same plays in the last four weeks that we called at the beginning of the season. There's been a lot of change. I think people probably don't understand all of it and don't see it and that's part of it. But we are fighting every day to put these guys in positions to go have success. The call sheet today looks completely different than it did week two, week three, week four. And I do mean completely different. Ain't good enough. It's not. Got to coach them better. Got to get them to take great care of the football and that will at least give us a chance to win a game. >> We've seen with Frisco the last few weeks that when the ball gets in the hands of these receivers, things happen. What's What's it been like dealing with that group and the frustrations that come with not being able to put the ball >> Yeah, it's it's frustrating. We've got guys that have the ability to to create chunks. We haven't been able to do that at near high enough clip to be able to again create more air in the run game. Part of it is our inability to have consistency in the run game as well. So those two things work hand in hand. We're going to need the run game next Saturday as we finish it out at home and we're going to need it, you know, the next two weeks. And that will take some pressure off of the quarterback position if we can find ways to sustain in the run game. >> And going back to your earlier comment about Camario, what was the conversation like with him and how have you seen the team respond knowing that number one is still number one for them moving forward? >> Yeah, you know, everybody in the building really excited when it when it came out. Everybody also in the building understood that K1's playing the entire time was coming back. And that conversation had been going inside our building for multiple weeks now. His messaging to his teammates and to myself and our staff is and he had full intentions on doing exactly what he did and and coming back. So, uh glad that that part is behind us now as we move it forward. >> Coach, from the start of the season to now, what kind of things have you seen from your team and the growth of your team throughout the season? >> Yeah, I there was a question earlier talking about effort. Um I've seen the guys every single day practice in in a really good way, far from perfect. But again, their energy and their intent in the building, how they work day in day out, their communication, how we've talked about, man, just continuing to tighten our circle. They've taken to that in a great way. Incredibly disappointed, frustrated in the result. I I've said it, not good enough. Our guys have been man, they've been great from the standpoint of working the right way, communicating the right way, having energy in our building and having belief in what we're doing. So, uh we're going to need that as we finish out the regular season. >> Appreciate it.
